Gripper failed to grasp-and-lift the test object on every shape
(cube) at 85% of its rated payload.
  Tested object mass: 4.250 kg (from the asset's authored custom:maxPayload)

This is the asset's grasp performance under FET028's standard
stress test (object diameter = 70% of maxOpening, friction = 2.0,
mass = 85% of rated maxPayload). When the test reaches this
point all the schema/topology checks above have already passed,
so the failure is in the asset's *authored physics* -- the
gripper closed and the lift was commanded, but the object
either slipped out, was knocked away, or was never gripped
firmly enough to follow the lift.

INSPECT THE METRICS for this run in result.json:
  - ``close_blocked_by_object_<shape>``  -- True means the
    fingers stopped on the object (good); False means they
    reached their upper limit with no contact (no grip).
  - ``object_lateral_drift_after_close_<shape>`` -- large values
    (> object_radius) mean the close knocked the object out.
  - ``vertical_follow_dz_m_<shape>`` -- > fall_min_delta_z
    means the object fell behind during the lift (slipped).
  - ``shake_max_relative_slip_m_<shape>`` (if shake enabled)
    -- > shake_max_relative_slip_m means the grip drifted under
    perturbation.

ASSET-AUTHORING LEVERS to investigate (in priority order):

  1. Finger-pad friction. Inspect the PhysicsMaterial bound to
     the finger pad collision meshes; static/dynamic friction
     below ~0.8 will let any reasonable object slip. Industrial
     pads typically author 1.0-2.0:
         float physics:staticFriction  = 1.5
         float physics:dynamicFriction = 1.5
     (FET006 covers this independently.)

  2. Master-mimic joint drive strength. The drive's
     ``stiffness`` and ``maxForce`` together determine the
     holding torque. As a starting point for a 5 kg payload
     parallel-jaw gripper:
         float drive:angular:physics:stiffness = 1000.0-5000.0
         float drive:angular:physics:damping   =   50.0-200.0
         float drive:angular:physics:maxForce  =  100.0-1000.0
     Too LOW = weak grip / object slips out. Too HIGH = fingers
     slam shut and knock the object away (look for large
     ``object_lateral_drift_after_close_<shape>``).

  3. ``custom:maxPayload`` honesty. If the heuristic was used
     (``used_heuristic_payload=True`` in metrics), the test
     guessed at the payload. Author a realistic value on the
     gripper site so future runs test the spec'd capability:
         custom float custom:maxPayload = 5.0   # kg

  4. Mimic relationship. Verify the mimic joints are bound to
     the master and their ratios make geometric sense -- a
     mis-wired mimic (wrong sign / ratio) can leave one pad
     out of contact while the master appears to close.

REFERENCE:
  Spec:      nv_core/sr_specs/docs/capabilities/physics_bodies/physics_grippers/requirements/
  Validator: nv_core/sr_specs/docs/capabilities/physics_bodies/physics_grippers/validation.py
  Example:   sample_content/common_assets/robots_general/Robotiq/2F-85/simready_isaac_usd/Robotiq_2F_85.usda
             (search for: def Xform "gripper_01")

MJC skipped: asset has only 1/6 joints with finite position limits; MJC needs at least 2.

WHAT THE TEST FOUND:
  - Articulation DOFs reported by Isaac: 6
  - DOFs with finite (lower, upper) and upper-lower > 1e-6: 1
  - Required by MJC: >= 2 (each driven independently to a mid-range
    target chosen by target_factors x [lower+margin, upper-margin]).

WHY IT MATTERS:
  MJC validates simultaneous multi-joint convergence under the PD
  drive controller. A revolute joint authored without limits (or
  with type='none', or as a continuous joint) has no mid-range
  target the test can pick, so it cannot participate.

FIX: On every joint you intend MJC to exercise, author finite
position limits on the matching axis. For PhysicsRevoluteJoint use
lowerLimit/upperLimit in DEGREES; for PhysicsPrismaticJoint use
lowerLimit/upperLimit in the stage's linear unit (typically meters).
Both must be finite and upperLimit > lowerLimit.

TEMPLATE -- paste/edit on each joint prim. Pick limits that match
the real mechanical travel of the joint; do NOT use +-inf:

    def PhysicsRevoluteJoint "joint_1"
    {
        uniform token physics:axis = "Z"
        float physics:lowerLimit = -170.0   # degrees
        float physics:upperLimit =  170.0   # degrees
        # ... body0 / body1 / localPos0 / localPos1 ...
    }

    def PhysicsPrismaticJoint "slider_1"
    {
        uniform token physics:axis = "X"
        float physics:lowerLimit = 0.0      # meters
        float physics:upperLimit = 0.085    # meters
        # ... body0 / body1 / localPos0 / localPos1 ...
    }

CHECKLIST per joint you expect MJC to drive:
  - physics:axis is set (X / Y / Z).
  - physics:lowerLimit and physics:upperLimit are BOTH finite.
  - physics:upperLimit - physics:lowerLimit > 1e-6 (non-degenerate).
  - Joint is reachable from the articulation root (otherwise Isaac
    will not expose it as a DOF; see FET_024 for articulation
    topology requirements).

If the joint is intentionally free-running (e.g. a passive wheel),
exclude it from your articulation rather than leaving it limit-less.
